item.title: Not introducing a special administration regime for English higher education providers will be a missed opportunity
item.description: We now have a sense of the government’s intended approach to possible university insolvencies. Neil Smyth takes a look

item.title: The missing infrastructure of racial equity in doctoral education
item.description: A programme supporting Black students into doctoral study is delivering results the sector has failed to achieve for decades. Ifedapo Francis Awolowo argues it's time to stop treating such work as exceptional and start treating it as evidence.

item.title: The Hickson review on university-investor links makes the case for commercialisation as a team sport
item.description: Tony Hickson's review into university-investor links is out and James Coe finds much to like on how culture, capital, and coordination can fuel the economy

item.title: Talking about contemporary higher education means talking about work-aligned learning
item.description: University study has never been more focused on labour market outcomes and local economic needs. Phil Power-Mason, Helen Charlton, Fran Walker-Martin and Sarah Bloomfield think through the vocabulary

item.title: Is the growth of international MRes recruitment a problem?
item.description: Though the numbers involved are small, last year saw a sharp rise in international recruitment to non-PhD research degrees. Mark Bennett asks what is going on

item.title: How will OfS respond in Sussex vs the Office for Students?
item.description: David Kernohan pulls out the key points from the Office for Students response to the judicial review of the processes that led to the decision to fine the University of Sussex

item.title: The Post-18 Project: A review of higher education funding is inevitable
item.description: As John Blake is announced as the first Director of The Post-18 Project, he argues that politicians must not ignore the feelings running ever deeper about the student loans system

item.title: Maybe a graduate tax wasn’t such a bad idea after all
item.description: Reflecting on continued coverage of Plan 2 graduates’ repayment woes, Jim Dickinson argues that a progressive graduate contribution scheme would be a better bet than the psychology of debt

item.title: What the Keep Britain Working review means for higher education
item.description: Overwork and staff illness have become central issues for the future of the sector. Helen Rimmer draws lessons from the government’s recent review of employment and ill-health

item.title: “Data steward” is just one of the missing 21st-century professions that universities could be creating
item.description: At King's College London the Data Empowerment Clinic is building a new profession: the data steward. Sylvie Delacroix posits the example as a model for other "missing" professional roles
